title: शिरीषको फूल र डापी उपन्यासमा अस्तित्ववादी निस्सारता
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेख पारिजातद्वारा लिखित शिरीषको फूल र ध्रुवचन्द्र गौतमद्वारा लिखित डापी उपन्यासको अस्तित्ववादी जीवनदृष्टिको मूलभूत मान्यता निस्सारताका कोणबाट गरिने तुलनात्मक अध्ययनमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । शिरीषको फूल र डापी उपन्यासमा अस्तित्ववादी निस्सारताको अभिव्यक्ति किन गरिएको हो भन्ने शोध्यप्रश्नको समाधानका लागि यी दुई उपन्यासको तुलनात्मक अध्ययन गरिने उद्देश्य यस अध्ययनमा राखिएको छ । स्वतन्त्र निर्णय गर्दै अस्तित्वका लागि प्रयत्नशील मानिसले भोग्नु परेका अनपेक्षित परिणाम, अभावजस्ता समस्याका कारण उसमा जीवनप्रति निरर्थकताको अनुभूति हुन्छ भन्ने मान्यता अस्तित्ववादी निस्सारताको रहेको छ । विवेच्य यी दुई उपन्यासका प्रमुख पात्रहरू सकमबरी, सुयोगवीर र विक्रमले अस्तित्वका लागि प्रयत्न गरिरहँदा भोग्नुपरेका अनपेक्षित परिणामका कारण निस्सारताको अनुभूति गरेको कुरालाई विषयबद्ध गरिएको छ । बहुसत्यमा विश्वास गरिएको यो गुणात्मक अध्ययनमा तत्त्वमीमांसा, ज्ञानमीमांसा र मूल्यमीमांसाका बीचमा समन्वय कायम गरिएको छ । पाठ विश्लेषण पद्धतिको अवलम्बन गरिएको यस अध्ययनमा उपन्यासका साक्ष्यका आधारमा निस्सारताको विश्लेषण गरिएकाले निगमनात्मक शोधविधि अवलम्बन गरिएको छ । अस्तित्वकालागि प्रयत्नशील मानिसले भोग्नुपर्ने समस्याका कारण उसमा जीवनप्रति निस्सारताको अनुभूति हुन्छ भन्ने लोकका लागि उपयोगी ज्ञानको सञ्चार यी दुई उपन्यासले गरेका छन् भन्ने निष्कर्ष यस अध्ययनको रहेको छ । अस्तित्ववादी निस्सारताको मर्म अनुकूल निर्मित उपकरणका आधारमायी दुई उपन्यासका बीचमा गरिएको तुलना नवीन, मौलिक र प्राज्ञिक दृष्टिले महत्वपूर्ण रहेकाले अन्य अध्येताका लागि उपयोगी हुनु यस अध्ययनको उपलब्धि रहेको छ ।
american_english: The present article is centered on a comparative study, from the angle of nihilism, of the fundamental tenet of the existentialist view of life in the novels Shirishko Phool, written by Parijat, and Dapi, written by Dhruba Chandra Gautam. This study sets the objective of making a comparative study of these two novels for the resolution of the research question of why the expression of existentialist nihilism was made in the novels Shirishko Phool and Dapi. The tenet of existentialist nihilism is that a person striving for existence while making free decisions comes to feel the meaninglessness of life because of problems such as the unexpected consequences and the lack that he has had to endure. The matter that the main characters of these two novels under discussion, Sakambari, Suyogbir and Bikram, felt nihilism because of the unexpected consequences they had to endure while striving for existence has been made the subject. In this qualitative study, which believes in multiple truths, a reconciliation has been established among metaphysics, epistemology and axiology. Since nihilism has been analyzed on the basis of the evidence of the novels in this study, which adopts the method of textual analysis, the deductive research method has been adopted. The conclusion of this study is that these two novels communicate knowledge useful to the world, that a person striving for existence feels the meaninglessness of life because of the problems he must endure. Since the comparison made between these two novels on the basis of instruments constructed in keeping with the essence of existentialist nihilism is important from a new, original and scholarly point of view, being useful to other scholars is the achievement of this study.

The belief behind existentialist nihilism is that someone who is having a go at existence while making free decisions ends up feeling life is pointless, because of dramas like the unexpected results and the lack they have had to cop. What has been made the subject here is the way the main characters of these two novels, Sakambari, Suyogbir and Bikram, felt a sense of pointlessness because of the unexpected results they had to cop while having a go at existence. In this qualitative study, which puts its faith in multiple truths, a balance has been kept among metaphysics, epistemology and axiology. Because the study, which takes up textual analysis, analyses nihilism on the basis of the evidence in the novels, it takes up the deductive research method. The study's conclusion is that these two novels get across knowledge that is useful to the world, that someone having a go at existence feels life is pointless because of the problems they have to cop. Because the comparison between these two novels, built on tools made to suit the guts of existentialist nihilism, matters from a new, original and scholarly angle, its being useful to other researchers is what this study has achieved.
